issues.description: Field Farm.animals: the problem statement (problem_statement.md) requires the Farm to use a List<Animal> backed by an ArrayList and to initialize the ArrayList in the no-argument constructor. The template (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) contains a TODO for implementing Farm and thus implies the student should follow the problem text. The solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) declares the field as private Queue<Animal> animals and initializes it with new LinkedList<>() in the constructor. This mismatch between the problem specification (List/ArrayList) and the provided solution (Queue/LinkedList) can confuse students about the expected attribute type, getter/setter signatures, and the exact constructor behavior to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent with the problem statement. Preferred fix: update the solution implementation to declare the field as private List<Animal> animals; import java.util.ArrayList and initialize animals = new ArrayList<>(); in the no-argument constructor; and change the getter and setter signatures to use List<Animal>. Update methods that iterate over animals accordingly. Alternative fix: relax the problem statement to accept any Collection/Queue implementation and remove the explicit 'ArrayList' requirement in the text (but ensure template and solution match the revised text).

issues.description: Concept: the Farm's collection of animals (the Farm.animals attribute). Problem statement: explicitly instructs using a List and initializing it with new ArrayList<>() in the no-arg constructor. Template repository: Farm.java contains a TODO and no concrete animals collection (class declaration and TODO at lines 3-4). Solution repository: Farm.java declares the field as Queue<Animal> and initializes it with new LinkedList<>(), with add/get methods using Queue semantics. This mismatch (List/ArrayList vs Queue/LinkedList, and the template lacking the specified List field) prevents students from clearly mapping the assignment instruction to the reference implementation and may cause confusion about the expected type for the animals collection, the required imports, and the getter/setter signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across artifacts. Update the solution (and the template) so the Farm declares the animals attribute as List<Animal> and initializes it in the no-arg constructor with new ArrayList<>(). Adjust the getter and setter signatures to use List<Animal>, update imports to java.util.List and java.util.ArrayList, and ensure addAnimal/feedAllAnimals/singFarmSong iterate over a List<Animal>. Alternatively, relax the problem statement to accept any Collection implementation and remove the explicit 'ArrayList' instruction; but prefer aligning solution/template to the stated List/ArrayList requirement.
